scenario.summary: NIK C2 is a Go-based Windows implant that uses a dual-channel C2 architecture over WebSockets and HTTP fallbacks to maintain persistent control. The framework notably integrates the OpenAI API directly through the victim host to analyze stolen data and orchestrate commands, while also supporting credential theft, hidden VNC, and screen-locking ransomware.

meta.rationale: Begin by examining hosts where binaries run from AppData/Roaming or Users/Public. NIK C2 relies on sub-paths like Microsoft\Network and masqueraded names like svchost.exe. Use the persistence_path parameter to match sub-folders found in your telemetry.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has established persistence for the NIK C2 implant by placing masqueraded binaries in user profile paths and creating Registry Run keys to maintain an AI-augmented remote access session.

hunt.name: NIK C2: Host Persistence and Evasion
hunt.description: This hunt targets the endpoint footprint of the NIK C2 implant, specifically its use of system process masquerading (svchost.exe, simvol.exe) and its watchdog supervisor routine. The hunt follows a phased flow: first, it identifies hosts with rare binaries in user-writable paths and checks for the implant's specific command-line arguments. Second, it corroborates these findings with Registry-based persistence mechanisms. Finally, an agent synthesizes the evidence to confirm the full malware lifecycle before an analyst takes action to prevent ransomware impact.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_path, process_cmd_line, COUNT(*) AS execution_count FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\public\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\roaming\%') AND LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%' || LOWER('{{persistence_path}}') || '%' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, process_path, process_cmd_line
config.description: Find hosts where processes are running from user profile paths matching the specific folder named in research.
config.expected_signal: Rows identify hosts and paths where binaries execute from the targeted Network directory. Silence proves these specific paths are clear.

primitive_config.label: Identify hosts with profile-path execution

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%watchdog%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%copywatchdog%') AND (instr(',' || '{{implant_masquerade_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(replace(process_path, rtrim(process_path, replace(process_path, '\', '')), '')) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find the specific Go-based watchdog tokens used by NIK C2 to monitor its masqueraded process.
config.expected_signal: A masqueraded process running with supervisor arguments. This is a high-fidelity indicator of NIK C2.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS runs, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\appdata\roaming\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\public\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(process_path) HAVING hosts < 3 ORDER BY hosts, runs
config.description: Stack-count profile binaries across the fleet so the implant stands out from normal updaters.
config.expected_signal: Binaries seen on only one or two hosts in the entire estate. Genuine system binaries should never appear here.
